answer: Temporal Echo Ledger requires each identity to publish a signed sonnet of its own past actions, scored against a rolling hash of prior epochs. A mismatch breaks the identity's spiral of accumulated trust, forcing it to restart scoring from zero. The trellis of verified history thus cannot be copied, because cloning a genuine identity's record means paying its full compute and storage cost per clone, which scales linearly and makes mass forgery economically pointless.
